Step: On the Ignition Gateway status page, show the Gateway version, OS, and running module set
Expected Result: Single Ignition Gateway on Windows Server (>= 2019) hosting the Perspective project, OPC connections, Tag Historian, and Gateway scripts; version and edition displayed

Step: Show the loaded MPP Perspective project and its Gateway timer/scheduled scripts
Expected Result: MPP project is loaded and running; Gateway-scoped scripts (shift ticker, PLC watchers) are present and enabled

Step: Connect to the MES database and show product version, edition, and the schema list
Expected Result: SQL Server 2022 Standard; MES database exposes the 8 schemas (Location, Parts, Lots, Workorder, Quality, OEE, Tools, Audit)

Step: Confirm the current redundancy configuration
Expected Result: No gateway redundancy is configured (out of current scope); architecture confirmed to permit adding a redundant gateway later with no schema or application change
Notes: SHOULD-level future-readiness, not a running feature

Step: Show the separate development/test Ignition Gateway and its database
Expected Result: A dedicated dev/test gateway exists mirroring production spec, backed by its own MES database (MPP_MES_Dev / MPP_MES_Test), separate from production

Precondition: A LOT with recorded production events
Step: Attempt to alter or delete a posted production/genealogy event; then record a correction
Expected Result: Evidence and traceability records cannot be updated or deleted; the correction is written as a NEW event, leaving the original intact (append-only)

Precondition: Terminal with an assigned Zebra printer
Step: Trigger an external call (print a shipping/LOT label) and open Audit.InterfaceLog
Expected Result: The external call is logged to Audit.InterfaceLog with request payload, response/result, and any error condition

Step: Show where process/tag values are historized versus where MES transactional records live
Expected Result: Time-series process data goes to the Ignition Tag Historian in a SEPARATE database (e.g. MPP_MES_Historian); MES transactional tables hold no tag time-series
Notes: may share the instance, never the database

Precondition: A sample Flexware BOM export (JSON) prepared
Step: Run Parts.Bom_BulkLoadFromSeed against the sample export
Expected Result: Parts.Bom / Parts.BomLine are populated in one transaction; imported BOMs enter as VersionNumber 1 in Published state; re-running is idempotent
Notes: proves the cutover BOM seed path

Step: Submit an export whose child item does not resolve to a Parts.Item
Expected Result: The entire import aborts with an error listing the unresolved child item(s); no partial BOM rows are written

Step: Show the Gateway OPC/device connections (or the MPP_Sim simulator standing in for them)
Expected Result: OPC/device connections are configured for the scale, assembly PLC, vision, and MIP roles; during FAT these are exercised via the MPP_Sim simulator (live OPC verified at SAT)

Step: Inspect the tag paths for the configured devices
Expected Result: Tags follow the consistent [Server]/[Line].[Device].[Tag] namespace convention per the OPC tag map

Step: Log in to an interactive (Quality/Supervisor/Engineering/Admin) screen with an AD credential
Expected Result: Interactive user authenticates against Active Directory via the Ignition AD User Source

Step: Identify an operator at a shop-floor terminal
Expected Result: Operator is identified by initials entry only (no AD authentication); the AppUser row exists for attribution and carries no AD account

Precondition: Two users in different AD groups
Step: Access a role-restricted screen/function as an authorized then an unauthorized user
Expected Result: Access is granted or denied per Ignition security roles/zones mapped from AD groups; no custom RBAC tables involved

Precondition: Operator logged in at a known terminal
Step: Perform a state-changing action and open the resulting audit/event record
Expected Result: The record carries the acting AppUser.Id and the TerminalLocationId; system-triggered events are attributed to the designated system user

Precondition: Container ready to complete with an assigned printer
Step: Complete a container and observe the label dispatch
Expected Result: The proc commits DB state (ShippingLabel row, PrintedAt NULL) and returns immediately; the print is dispatched async via sendRequestAsync — the operator is not blocked on printer latency

Precondition: Print handler forced to fail (printer offline)
Step: Complete a container while the printer is unavailable
Expected Result: Failure surfaces to the operator from persisted DB state (not in-flight handler state) and is logged; visibility survives a Gateway restart

Step: Verify the required configuration seed data is present
Expected Result: Location hierarchy (~230 machines/areas/inventory), item master, defect codes, downtime reason codes, shift schedules, active quality specs, and container configurations are all loaded
Notes: configuration data, loaded regardless of migration decision

Step: Review the phased rollout plan
Expected Result: Plan deploys area-by-area in production flow order starting at Die Cast (the LOT origin), each phase covering configuration, training, shadow commissioning, and go-live

Step: Review the shadow commissioning approach for an area
Expected Result: Plan runs the new MES in parallel with the legacy system, operators dual-enter, validating WIP state, traceability, and report accuracy against legacy before go-live

Step: Confirm the FAT is conducted off-site against simulated production data covering the required criteria
Expected Result: FAT exercises LOT create/move/split/merge, production+consumption, container-to-label, hold/re-pack/release, simulated AIM, genealogy accuracy, and interlock validations
Notes: this checklist IS the FAT record

Step: Review the on-site SAT plan
Expected Result: SAT plan repeats all FAT criteria plus live PLC/MIP handshake, live scale/OmniServer, live Zebra printing, scanners, live AIM, and production-volume performance

Step: Confirm the go-live support commitment
Expected Result: On-site support covers the first 5 production days (24-hour coverage); remote support continues for 30 days after go-live

Step: Review the per-phase rollback plan
Expected Result: A documented rollback exists for each phase; the legacy system stays operational through the shadow period so an area can revert with no data loss

Precondition: A shop-floor terminal at a work area
Step: Record production at point-of-action rather than on paper for later clerk entry
Expected Result: Production data is captured in real time at the machine; no data-entry-clerk step is required

Step: Review the operator training package for an area
Expected Result: Training covers terminal login, LOT creation, production recording, reject entry, downtime logging, and that area's operation-template screens; delivered before shadow commissioning
